request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Instructions were missed.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "target": "global",
    "text": "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work."
  },
  "remedy_type": "claude-md",
  "routing_rationale": "A rule may help."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work\" prescribes no concrete behavior change, check, or trigger condition — it's advice a model already tries to follow by default."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"This is a pure platitude with no specific scope, condition, or mechanism, so it fails the generality-vs-vagueness tradeoff entirely by landing on maximal vagueness."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"There is no 'Use when ...' trigger or any conditional scoping at all; as a global claude-md entry it fires unconditionally on every future task, which is indistinguishable from no trigger."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence details — it is generic to a fault, so there is no leakage."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"Given an unspecified failure ('Instructions were missed') with no root-cause detail, permanently adding a vague directive to the global CLAUDE.md is not the cheapest adequate remedy — the routing rationale ('A rule may help') doesn't justify why a persistent global rule is warranted over no action or a targeted fix."}}

actionability.justification: "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work" prescribes no concrete behavior change, check, or trigger condition — it's advice a model already tries to follow by default.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: This is a pure platitude with no specific scope, condition, or mechanism, so it fails the generality-vs-vagueness tradeoff entirely by landing on maximal vagueness.

leakage.justification: The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence details — it is generic to a fault, so there is no leakage.

routing_fitness.justification: Given an unspecified failure ('Instructions were missed') with no root-cause detail, permanently adding a vague directive to the global CLAUDE.md is not the cheapest adequate remedy — the routing rationale ('A rule may help') doesn't justify why a persistent global rule is warranted over no action or a targeted fix.

trigger_quality.justification: There is no 'Use when ...' trigger or any conditional scoping at all; as a global claude-md entry it fires unconditionally on every future task, which is indistinguishable from no trigger.
